avoid_angles: abstract invisible quantum field jargon without vivid visuals
physics.hook_style: Use 'The [Concrete Object] Paradox' or impossible-sounding physical contrast in title & beat 1
physics.extra_directive: Prioritize phenomena viewers can instantly visualize (glass, ice, magnets, water, extreme pressure) over abstract equations.

focus_topics: extreme thermal/phase-change contrasts (hot ice, liquid metals, supercooled liquids)
dramatic visible reactions and strange elements
everyday materials with shocking hidden chemistry
avoid_angles: vague 'changes color' titles without extreme stakes
chemistry.hook_style: Use extreme physical contrast titles like 'The [Substance] That [Impossible Action]!'
chemistry.extra_directive: Lead with the most extreme sensory contrast (burning cold, metal that melts in your hand, liquid that climbs walls).

focus_topics: extreme ocean and wildlife superpowers (camouflage, regeneration, bioluminescence)
weird real survival adaptations with vivid nature footage
avoid_angles: confusing metaphors or clickbait-sounding exaggerations in titles
biology.hook_style: Spotlight one concrete creature's superpower: 'The [Habitat]'s Ultimate [Superpower]!'
biology.extra_directive: Keep titles literal, vivid, and anchored to a real animal, plant, or ocean organism.

focus_topics: gravity-defying liquids and impossible-looking everyday physics/nature
high-curiosity natural anomalies and surprising engineering breakthroughs
general_science.hook_style: Use curiosity-gap 'The [Thing] That [Defies/Breaks Rule]!' titles instead of 'Why...'
general_science.extra_directive: Avoid school-lesson phrasing. Frame every topic as a baffling real-world anomaly revealed in 20 seconds.

focus_topics: deep Earth mysteries, ancient geological time capsules, extreme volcanoes, ocean trenches
extreme exoplanets (metal rain, diamond rain, rogue worlds), black holes, neutron stars
astronomy.hook_style: Keep winning 'The Alien World / Star That [Extreme Phenomenon]' framing
